items.title: Unpatched Magento and Adobe Commerce Zero-Day Exploited to Backdoor Online Stores
items.one_liner: An unpatched zero-day in Magento and Adobe Commerce is being exploited to gain remote code execution, with no official fix currently available.
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce, dubbed 'StyleSmuggler,' is being actively exploited to backdoor online stores. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server, and researchers report that patching status is currently irrelevant as the exploit bypasses existing security measures. Adobe has not yet released a patch or CVE identifier, leading security firms to recommend temporarily disabling GraphQL as a mitigation. Multiple stores have already been compromised, with attackers installing persistent backdoors.
items.bottom_line: If you run Magento or Adobe Commerce, you are currently vulnerable to unauthenticated RCE; disable GraphQL immediately if you do not rely on it for your storefront.

items.title: Active crypto address "copy and paste attack" threatens users even after major malware cleanup cut off hackers
items.one_liner: Sality botnet's command infrastructure was disrupted, but local EggJagger crypto-swapping malware remains active on infected systems.
items.summary: A multinational law enforcement operation on August 31, 2026, disrupted the Sality botnet by seizing domains and establishing sinkholes, cutting off its ability to deliver new payloads to over 33,000 infected machines worldwide. However, malware already present on compromised systems—specifically the EggJagger clipboard-monitoring tool—remains active and continues to perform cryptocurrency address-swapping attacks. Because the botnet takedown did not automatically remove local files, infected users must manually remediate their systems to prevent stolen funds. Cybersecurity firms and agencies recommend checking network telemetry for specific UDP traffic and using provided YARA rules to detect lingering infections. Coordinated efforts by entities like the Shadowserver Foundation are underway to notify victims and assist with remediation.
items.bottom_line: Disrupting a botnet's command-and-control infrastructure does not remove resident payloads like crypto-swapping malware, leaving user funds at risk until manual remediation occurs.
